title: A textbook age band and a CDC checklist line are not the same measurement
summary: OpenStax gives a five-to-eight-month band for object permanence, while the CDC lists looking for a dropped object by nine months and a hidden toy by one year as separate checklist items.
body: OpenStax Psychology puts the hidden-object understanding between five and eight months in its Piaget section. The CDC, a different publisher, lists two behaviors: by nine months, most babies look for an object dropped out of sight, and by one year, most babies look for a toy they saw hidden. One source is a theory band. The other is a checklist of what most children do. This reading does not average them into a single age, and it does not treat the checklist as a test of the textbook's term.
